contract.tracking: VCD off; coverage off; profiling off; recorder and validation outside phase timing
contract.stop_rule: One fixed round. Stop on timeout or behavior mismatch; publish failures. No optimization or extra workload.

retained_launch_issue: Initial recorder had a five-minute outer timeout. Completed samples retained exactly; continuation uses the original round deadline and no sample is discarded or resampled.
limits: One host, warm filesystem caches; each sample is a fresh interpreter/kernel.
Same installed dependencies and native SystemC; revision source trees are frozen and guarded.
Python driver/checksum work is included in simulation timing; assertions and recorder I/O are outside phase timing.
TLM workload uses a reused payload and nonwaiting address transform with delay annotation, not a memory or thread-throughput model.
Native preflight uses shared Python stimulus; selected behavior equivalence does not certify every API.
No single package-wide percentage; no timing percentages summed; no optimization adopted.

Both revisions emit native W509 in the TLM workload because the retained top sc_module_name leaves construction open until sc_start. Values, callbacks and time are checked; this benchmark does not verify module-construction lifecycle contracts.
Revision differences include correctness and API changes as well as optimizations; timing does not isolate individual optimization commits.
Process wall includes post-run assertions, native-library hashing, import guards, shutdown and temporary-directory handling; import/elaboration/run phase timing excludes final assertions.
